note: [agent-bulk] shw 10051 (120.4 MeV kine_charge / 72.4 kine_best, 1 seg, pdg 11, mcp2k nuecc): under-clustered, and the mechanism is SPLITTING rather than a missed neighbour. This event is ONE broad EM shower -- a single continuous point cloud fanning out of the neutrino vertex over ~40 cm, the textbook nuecc electron, and the star sits exactly at its apex, so the vertex is good (native framing, 51.4 cm half-span, no re-frame needed). The reconstruction threads that one cloud with SEVEN overlapping polylines all starting on the vertex, and turns four of them into four separate showers: 10051 (21.3 cm), 10052 (23.5 cm), 10054 (29.1 cm) and 10056 (24.8 cm), plus three left unowned -- 10050 (17.6 cm, pdg 211), 10057 (29.6 cm, pdg 13) and 10012 (4.0 cm, pdg 2212). Every one of them is in cluster 10 and every one reads dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 against every other, which is the display's degenerate readout for exactly this situation. It is visible in one frame: in shw10051-az-055-el+20 and again from 140 deg away in shw10051-az+085-el+20, the yellow member halo covers only the short blue strand near the apex while orange, green, red, grey and purple strands run through the SAME cloud beside it. So the verdict shower holds roughly one seventh of an object it should hold all of. Marked IN: 10052, 10054, 10056 -- the three cluster-10 strands that are other showers' seeds. Two caveats on those marks, stated because they matter for how the mark is read. (1) I marked only the three SEEDS, not the cluster-36/37/38 fragments those showers also own (36038, 37039, 38041 under 10054; 38042, 38043 under 10052), because those live in the detached blob 33-41 cm out beyond a visible gap and whether that blob belongs is a separate question I did not settle. (2) I did NOT mark the unowned strands 10050 and 10057 even though they run through the same charge, because they carry pdg 211 and 13 tags, i.e. the reconstruction is holding them as track hypotheses, and marking them would be a PID statement dressed up as a clustering one. If the summed shower energies here are ever used as a total, note that four showers threading one cloud is a double-counting hazard: 120.4 + 106.3 + 75.5 + 23.9 = 326 MeV of kine_charge assigned to a single ~40 cm nuecc shower. I did not verify how the code shares charge between overlapping segments, so treat that as a flag to check, not as a measurement. Confidence likely rather than certain: the picture is unambiguous that this is one object, but I cannot rule out that the four-strand structure is deliberate (one shower per Steiner-tree branch) rather than a failure, and that is a code question, not a picture question. No reco pi0 group and no second EM object anywhere in the event, so nothing to pair. Clustering statement, silent on PID. Showers NOT looked at: the 5 the scope rule skipped -- 10001 (5.0 MeV), 16034 (2.0), 18036 (0.8), 17035 (0.8), 35037 (0.2).
